name: Zinc for body odor
lead: Zinc for body odor refers to the claim, circulated in supplement and appearance communities, that taking zinc orally reduces body odor. Zinc is an essential mineral; oral forms such as zinc gluconate and zinc acetate are used to treat or prevent zinc deficiency.[1]
The reference pages consulted for this entry describe body odor as arising mainly from bacterial breakdown of sweat gland secretions and do not mention zinc as a factor or treatment.[2]

paras: Body odor is attributed chiefly to skin bacteria acting on apocrine sweat, with genetics (such as ABCC11), diet and health also contributing.[2] Standard treatments listed include antiperspirants, deodorants and bathing.[2]

card.summary: Oral zinc is sometimes claimed to cut body odor; the sources consulted give no support for this use.
card.note: Thin evidence; zinc is established only for deficiency.

quick.overview:
Zinc is an essential mineral sold as an over-the-counter supplement. Some online discussion links it to reduced body odor.

The sources consulted do not mention zinc in connection with body odor.
quick.mechanism: Proponents' mechanism is not documented in the sources consulted. Body odor is generally attributed to bacteria acting on sweat.
quick.risks: Not assessed in the sources consulted for this use. Oral zinc is used for deficiency repletion.
